title: Visual analysis
description: The machine-readable half of the reference analysis, at examples/<project>/revisions/<id>/visual-analysis.json. It carries the parts later stages have to address by name — the named regions, the relational geometry, the anchor relationships, the shape-ownership cases and the open questions. visual-analysis.md keeps the prose observations. Per skills/workflows/create-template/SKILL.md the analysis describes the page in RATIOS and DEPENDENCIES, not pixels, and it must not pick GraphCompose primitives — that is the Architecture Mapper's job.

schemaVersion.description: On-disk contract version for this artifact.

margins.description: Margins expressed relationally where possible, e.g. "~7% of page width".

regions.description: Named regions of the reference, in reading order. Every later artifact addresses regions by these ids: architecture-plan.json maps region -> render method, and visual-review.json reports mismatches per region.

contains.description: Elements inside the region, named the way a reader would name them.

proportions.description: The region's share of its parent, as a ratio or weight — never a pixel width. E.g. "0.31 of the content row".

bounds.description: The region as FRACTIONS of the page, top-left origin. Optional but cheap — four numbers — and it is what makes the region croppable: crop-region projects one fractional rect onto the reference and the render, whatever their resolutions, so a correction pass reads two small crops instead of two full pages. A region without bounds cannot be cropped, and the tool refuses rather than guessing.

role.description: What the region IS to the page, not what it contains. Required: a region with no role states no contract for how it may be built, and check-region-primitives cannot check it. page-header / page-footer are chrome that repeats on every page and must map to DocumentSession.header/.footer (or the version equivalent), never be drawn as body content and never bleedToEdge, which extends a fill past the margin to the paper edge. table-header repeats at the top of every page its table reaches (TableBuilder.repeatHeader). table must be built with addTable, not as rows of shapes. image must use addImage and icon addSvgIcon — a filled rectangle or a coloured disc standing in for either matches the box and nothing inside it. background is page-level fill behind everything; panel, divider and content carry no build contract.

layoutProportions.description: The page described in ratios and dependencies. Base constants derived from these land in architecture-plan.json.

anchors.description: Every element whose placement depends on another element, stated as a relationship rather than an offset. The Architecture Mapper turns each into a named engine primitive (LayerAlign, TextAlign, weights(...), ...).

relationship.description: E.g. "centred on", "pinned to the top-right of", "baseline-aligned with".

region.description: Region id this anchor belongs to.

shapeOwnership.description: Mandatory for the five cases skills/workflows/create-template/SKILL.md names: initials or icons inside circles, text inside pills or badges, content inside rounded cards, images clipped by rounded or circular shapes, and badges anchored inside or on a shape boundary.

colors.description: Colour roles rather than a raw swatch list, so the theme tokens in architecture-plan.json have something to map to.

assets.description: What the Asset Resolver will have to fetch. The authoritative request is asset-request.json.

unclearParts.description: Where the reference could not be read with confidence. skills/workflows/create-template/SKILL.md forbids silently guessing, so an assumption recorded here is the contract for what was assumed.

notes.description: Prose the rest of this schema cannot carry — a table comparing revisions, a paragraph of causal reasoning — emitted verbatim by scripts/render-artifact-md.mjs under a Notes heading. Markdown blocks. This exists so the reading copy stays generated: narrative belongs here, not in a hand-written .md twin that can disagree with this file.

flow.description: The fixed-vs-flowing decision, made explicitly at analysis time. A one-page invoice SCREENSHOT is not a one-page DOCUMENT: the sample shows four line items, real data brings thirty, and a template built as a fixed page breaks on the first real dataset. Recording the decision here is what forces the question to be asked while the reference is in front of the analyst, not after the first overflow bug.

kind.description: fixed: the page IS the artifact (CV, certificate, poster) - content is curated to fit. flowing: content volume is data-driven (invoice line items, transactions, an article) and the layout must paginate.

drivenBy.description: For flowing documents: the region id whose content grows with real data, e.g. line-items.

overflowExpectation.description: One sentence of reasoning: why real data will or will not spill past the page the reference shows. This is the sentence that decides whether the example data must include enough rows to reach page 2.

pageEnumeration.description: Whether the reader has to be able to tell that a page is missing. It is not decoration and it is not for every document: an invoice, a statement, an estimate, a formal proposal or a report is a record someone may print, post or file, and a page that vanishes from it should be detectable. A CV or a poster does not carry that duty. Recording the decision structurally is what stops it being made by whether the analyst happened to notice a page number in the reference.

required.description: true when a missing page must be detectable from the page itself.

reason.description: One sentence: why this document does or does not carry that duty.

location.description: Which chrome zone carries it. Maps to DocumentSession.footer(...) / .header(...) with DocumentHeaderFooterZone.

format.description: The literal chrome text, with GraphCompose's placeholders, e.g. "Page {page} of {pages}". The {pages} half is the part that makes a missing page detectable; "Page 3" alone does not.

repeat.description: every-page is the default. after-first suppresses it on a cover page, via DocumentPageNumbering.showOnFirstPage(false).

then.description: A flowing document has more than one page in its future, so whether the reader can tell a page is missing is a decision someone has to make. Requiring the field forces it to be made rather than defaulted by omission; recording `required: false` with a reason is a perfectly good answer.
